description: Local web application sharing companion that creates temporary Cloudflare Quick Tunnels

script: if ($sourceDirs.Count -ne 1) { throw 'Could not identify the Yerel source directory in the downloaded archive.' }
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Yerel npm dependency installation failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE." }
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Yerel Next.js production build failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE." }
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $sourceRoot '.next') -PathType Container)) { throw 'Yerel build did not produce the expected .next directory.' }

post_install: if ($sourceDirs.Count -ne 1) { throw 'Yerel production build directory was not found.' }
$companionShortcut.Description = 'Start the Yerel local companion and Cloudflare tunnel controller'
notes: This is a source-based Windows build pinned to a full upstream Git commit; installation runs npm ci and a Next.js production build.
Use the Yerel Companion shortcut first. It prints a session-specific pairing token and listens on 127.0.0.1:3847. Then start Yerel Web and open http://127.0.0.1:3000; enter the token to pair.
The app requires the cloudflared dependency and starts a temporary public Cloudflare Quick Tunnel only after the user enters a local target and explicitly confirms sharing.
The upstream repository currently has no declared license or LICENSE file, so the manifest uses Unknown. Review status remains until a Windows install/build and live launch are verified.
The upstream does not publish a checksum for source archives; the manifest pins the downloaded source to a full commit SHA.
